summary: This House resolution recognizes linemen as first responders who maintain power lines and protect public safety, and expresses support for designating April 18, 2026, as National Lineman Appreciation Day.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a purely symbolic measure recognizing linemen and designating a national day of appreciation. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill makes no reference to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No content in the resolution addresses healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the text pertains to immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
The resolution does not engage with reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
While linemen maintain energy infrastructure, the bill is limited to recognition and does not propose or alter any environmental regulations or climate policies.
The measure contains no references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No elements of the resolution address schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no bearing on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
Nothing in the text concerns sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The resolution does not address trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal policy, deficits, or debt reduction measures are mentioned.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No content pertains to foreign assistance or international aid.
The resolution does not engage with voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No references to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight appear in the bill.
Although linemen often belong to unions, the resolution is strictly honorary and introduces no labor policy, union rights, or workplace regulations.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination measures.
